title: [M5] Maintenance: Athena OPTIMIZE/VACUUM + supersession reconciliation
description:
Implement `maintenance/optimize.py` + `entrypoints/maintenance.py` per §9.4 (weekly, three steps, each polled to completion; any failure → raise → Lambda error → alarm). Step 1: OPTIMIZE <db>.delivery_ledger REWRITE DATA USING BIN_PACK. Step 2: VACUUM <db>.delivery_ledger — retention is governed by the table properties create_ledger.py set at bootstrap (already done in M2); do not set retention here. Step 3: supersession reconciliation — the repair for §8.3's named concurrent-correction race: query for delivery_keys with more than one live registered delivery (the latest-disposition fold in SQL, same shape as the current-dispositions named query §11.4), feed the result to the pure planner plan_reconciliation (already implemented in core/decisions.py by m1-folds-planners) and perform ONE fx.ledger.append of the resulting superseded accretion rows; SupersessionsReconciled metric; idempotent via append-on-change. Athena interaction: no Athena record exists in §7.7 and moto cannot simulate Athena adequately — put the start/poll/results calls behind a small local record of functions inside the maintenance module (same records-of-functions idiom, §7.0 rule 3) so the polling/sequencing logic is testable with a fake record; document the moto exclusion inline per §12.5. Note the boto3 athena client usage lives in this module or a tiny effects/athena.py — either is acceptable; it is effect-side code, exempt from purity rules but NOT from idiom rules. Tests: polling/sequencing against the fake athena record (success, query failure → raise, timeout); reconciliation end-to-end against the local ledger — seed two live registered rows for one delivery_key, run step 3 with the query replaced by the local fold, assert the accretion row and that a second run appends nothing. Terraform (M6) will make this function's role the only principal with s3:DeleteObject on the ledger prefix — nothing to do in code. Runs parallel with m5-absence — do not touch absence/, effects/records.py, or conftest.py.

FILES (ownership): ingestion/ingestion/maintenance/optimize.py, ingestion/ingestion/entrypoints/maintenance.py, ingestion/tests/golden/test_reconciliation.py, ingestion/tests/unit/test_maintenance.py
acceptance_criteria: Reconciliation golden test green (accretion row appended once; second run is a no-op); polling-logic tests green against the fake athena record; full `make test` green; `make lint` green.
notes:
M1 handoff: plan_reconciliation(live_duplicates) takes Mapping[str, Sequence[DeliveryRecord]] PRE-GROUPED by delivery_key — maintenance must group the Athena/scan result before calling.
M3 handoff addition: when building 9.4 reconciliation append, add maintenance/optimize.py to tests/golden/test_ownership.py::_ALLOWED_CALLERS — the ownership test fails otherwise by design.

title: [M4] sftp-pull driver + golden suite (G-02/05b/05c/06-sftp/10/13) + driver stubs
description:
Implement `drivers/sftp_pull.py` acquire(feed, window, fx) per the §9.2 normative walk and the §7.6 driver contract, plus `entrypoints/sftp_pull.py` (wiring only; payload {} | {window, force} | {resume_batch_id}). Step 0 resume: load claim item, verify objects_inventory present at canonical uris, rebuild RegistrationRequest from the item, enter register_delivery (claim returns TAKEN_OVER, resumes E1–E5). Main path: scan_feed since now − lookback (env var, default 45 d — read effect-side, simplest gap resolution) → acquired_final / observed_defective folds → sftp_fx_for(secret_ref) → listdir → optional window filter on mtime. Manifest mode: select_manifests (non-final manifests re-examined every run by design); remote manifest read ≤ 1 MiB → parse failure → record_nondelivery(unreadable, key=basename); parts missing/size-mismatched in listing → record_nondelivery(incomplete, observed = listing ∩ manifest); else mint received_at + delivery_id, stream each part AND the manifest via stream_upload(sftp.read_chunks) — hashed en route, streamed sha256 != manifest sha256 → record_nondelivery(unreadable) and abandon; evaluate_manifest → RegistrationRequest (src_key=None) → register_delivery. Trailer/timer: select_candidates; stream to canonical; trailer verifies via get_tail on the STREAMED object; timer is complete by selection. ORDERING (deliberate, §9.2 note): streaming to canonical keys happens BEFORE the claim — batch_id needs the hash; orphaned canonical prefixes from duplicate losers are accepted and documented by the duplicate row's objects column. Budget: stop starting new deliveries after 10 min elapsed or bytes > budget (env, default 5 GiB); log carry-over + DriverCarryOver metric. Failure isolation: per-delivery exceptions caught at the loop boundary; TransientErrors re-raised AFTER the loop so the run fails and alarms without blocking other deliveries. Also: `drivers/api_pull.py` and `db_unload.py` become `raise NotImplementedError` stubs with a comment pointing at LLD §1 (FeedConfig already rejects them). Fixtures for carrier-x (§15.1): 2-part delivery + native manifest, corrected re-send pair, incomplete manifest. Golden: G-02 happy trailer file; G-05b identical file re-listed on scheduled path — ZERO new rows (selection no-op, D-16); G-05c force re-pull — duplicate rows explain each skip, no events; G-06 sftp variant — supersession; G-10 operator window re-pull over acquired window — zero new registered rows; G-13 quiet-window — too-fresh file skipped, next run (advance the fixture clock) picks it up. ABSTRACTION GATE (§13): if this bead requires ANY edit inside registration/ or effects/ beyond adding the caller, STOP and surface it — the §7.6 interface is wrong and must be revisited before proceeding, not patched around.

FILES (ownership): ingestion/ingestion/drivers/sftp_pull.py, ingestion/ingestion/entrypoints/sftp_pull.py, ingestion/ingestion/drivers/api_pull.py, ingestion/ingestion/drivers/db_unload.py, ingestion/tests/golden/test_sftp_pull.py, ingestion/sources/carrier-x/commission-statements/tests/fixtures/
acceptance_criteria: G-02, G-05b, G-05c, G-06 (sftp variant), G-10, G-13 green under `make test-golden`; zero diffs inside ingestion/registration/ and ingestion/effects/ in this bead's change set (the two-driver abstraction test); `make lint test` green.
notes: M3 handoff for this bead: reuse registration.registrar.register_delivery / record_nondelivery EXACTLY as built — record_nondelivery takes driver_run_id (current invocation, from context.aws_request_id); execute takes run_id (same). registrar._trigger_for is already driver-agnostic. Read ingestion/.claude/agent-memory/senior-de/m3-registration-s3push-design-notes.md first.

title: [M5] Absence detector: overdue sweep + stuck-claim sweep (G-12/G-12b)
description:
Implement `absence/detector.py` + `entrypoints/absence.py` per §9.3 (hourly). For each registry feed with an expectation (feeds.json only, §6.8): overdue_dates(exp, received_at list from registered_deliveries fold of scan_feed(feed, since=now−5d), now); for each overdue date, EMIT-THEN-MARK: if not marker_exists('overdue#<feed_id>#<date>') → emit delivery-overdue + OverdueEmitted metric → mark (False = lost race, fine). The order is normative — mark-then-emit was explicitly rejected because a crash after marking loses the signal permanently; at-least-once with consumer dedup on (feed_id, expectation_date) is the contract (D-14). Then the stuck-claim sweep: for each item in cas.sweep_stale(now), route on item.driver — s3-push → async invoke ${p}-registrar with a synthetic event rebuilt from item.trigger; sftp-pull → async invoke ${p}-driver-<slug> with {resume_batch_id: item.batch_id}; StuckClaimsRecovered metric + WARNING log with the claim item. NAMED INTERFACE GAP: §9.3 requires Lambda invocation but the §7.7 Effects record has no such capability — add ONE additive field (e.g. invoke_async: Callable[[str, dict], None]) to effects/records.py, wire it in build.py (boto3 lambda client) and as a recording local function in the conftest fixture; keep it minimal, do not build a general invocation abstraction. This is the sanctioned, pre-planned accretion — coordinate nothing else in records.py. Golden: G-12 weekday feed, no delivery by deadline → exactly one delivery-overdue; G-12b second sweep emits nothing (marker holds); plus a sweep test proving a pre-seeded stale sftp claim routes a resume invoke to the right function name and an s3-push claim routes a synthetic event to the registrar (closing the loop G-11 opened in M3). This bead runs in parallel with m5-maintenance — do not touch maintenance/ or core/decisions.py. M5 gate: full `make test` green.

FILES (ownership): ingestion/ingestion/absence/detector.py, ingestion/ingestion/entrypoints/absence.py, ingestion/ingestion/effects/records.py, ingestion/ingestion/effects/build.py, ingestion/tests/conftest.py, ingestion/tests/golden/test_absence.py
acceptance_criteria: G-12 and G-12b green under `make test-golden`; sweep-routing golden test green (both driver routes); full `make test` green; `make lint` green.
notes: M4 handoff: stuck-claim sweep invokes per-feed driver Lambda with payload exactly {"resume_batch_id": item.batch_id}; route on item.driver (s3-push -> registrar with synthetic event from item.trigger). NOTE: registrar._trigger_for currently records {"src_keys": []} for sftp-pull (window not persisted) — resume path does not need it (resumer re-derives via sweep_stale), but your synthetic-event build for s3-push DOES read item.trigger. Effects async-invoke capability: add the minimal additive field to Effects per the architect plan (records.py/build.py/conftest.py are in your FILES).

title: [M3] Registration core, s3-push path, and the s3-push golden suite (G-01/03/04/05a/06/07/08/11)
description:
The turnstile milestone. `registration/registrar.py` (§8, §8.5 normative): exactly three functions — register_delivery (claim → plan_registration(claim, scan_feed, req, now) → execute), record_nondelivery (plan_nondelivery → execute; the non-turnstile path for incomplete/unreadable — both RETURN SUCCESS, recorded not retried), and execute (the interpreter: E1 copies, E2 single ledger append, E3 event, E4 complete claim, E5 metrics — fixed order, no judgment; a conditional beyond the four `if plan.x` guards is the design eroding, §8.5). `drivers/s3_push.py` + `entrypoints/registrar_s3.py` (§8.2): parse event → derive feed_id from key → load FeedConfig from the registry object (artifacts bucket, cached per container ≤ 60 s, §6.8 — never from filesystem); manifest mode: get_bytes (1 MiB cap) → parse_manifest (Defect → record_nondelivery(unreadable), delivery_key = manifest basename) → list vestibule → stream_sha256 declared-present files → evaluate_manifest (incomplete → record_nondelivery + stop, no retry — §8.2 explains why); trailer mode: single object, stream_sha256 + get_tail → evaluate_trailer; then mint received_at/delivery_id/content_hash/batch_id, build StagedObjects with canonical target URIs and vestibule src_keys — NO canonical write before the claim; the vestibule→canonical copy happens only inside execute E1, so a race loser never copies; vestibule objects are never deleted by code (D-3). Entrypoint is wiring only (§7.1). Add the small observability helper (§11.1 20-line JSON formatter + §11.2 EMF metric dict printer, namespace Conveyer/Ingestion, dimension feed_id) as one effect-side module — LLD gives it no file; `ingestion/observability.py` is the simplest consistent home; keep it out of core/. Golden suite (drives the REAL handler with synthetic S3→EventBridge events shaped per §10.7 against local_effects): G-01 happy manifest (2 parts) — 1 registered row, canonical objects present, 1 event; G-03 duplicate sequential event — registered + duplicate rows, 1 event; G-04 concurrent race via an injected CasFx interleaving — one WON→registered, one LOST_IN_PROGRESS→duplicate, both sides remembered, 1 event; G-05a identical re-send — duplicate row, no event; G-06 corrected re-send — new registered with supersedes + accreted superseded row, 1 new event; G-07 missing part — incomplete row, no copy, no event; G-08 sha256 mismatch — unreadable, no event; G-11 crash-after-claim — pre-seed a stale in_progress claim, re-invoke the handler, assert TAKEN_OVER resumes the dead run's exact identity and the fold shows exactly one registered (full sweep routing arrives in M5). Per §8.3, G-03/04/06/11 assert the PLAN first (exact rows/copies/event), then run the interpreter and assert the world agrees. Also ship the ownership grep test (§8: call sites of ledger.append/emit exist only in registrar.py and §9.4's reconciliation) and the carrier-y fixture set (§15.2: happy multi-part, duplicate replay, sha256 mismatch). Do NOT touch core/decisions.py (planners are done; if a plan shape is wrong, surface it), and do NOT add driver-specific branches inside registration/ (§7.6 abstraction rule).

FILES (ownership): ingestion/ingestion/registration/registrar.py, ingestion/ingestion/drivers/s3_push.py, ingestion/ingestion/entrypoints/registrar_s3.py, ingestion/ingestion/observability.py, ingestion/tests/golden/test_s3_push_registration.py, ingestion/tests/golden/test_ownership.py, ingestion/sources/carrier-y/renewal-statements/tests/fixtures/
acceptance_criteria: G-01, G-03, G-04, G-05a, G-06, G-07, G-08, G-11 green under `make test-golden`; ownership grep test green; execute() contains no conditionals beyond the four plan guards (reviewed); `make lint test-unit test-integration` stay green.
notes:
M1 handoff for this bead: (1) plan_nondelivery signature grew delivery_id + driver_run_id params (non-nullable ledger columns; caller mints fresh delivery_id per call via new_delivery_id()); (2) RegistrationRequest/CopySpec/RegistrationPlan live in core/decisions.py; (3) s3-push duplicate-row vestibule 'uris' are bare src_key strings (no bucket in pure inputs) — if M3 wants full s3:// URIs, put the bucket into StagedObject.src_key at request-build time rather than widening planner inputs; (4) TAKEN_OVER supersession scan excludes dead run's own row by delivery_id. Details in ingestion/.claude/agent-memory/senior-de/m1-folds-planners-design-notes.md.
M2 handoff for this bead: (1) CAS TAKEN_OVER asymmetry is load-bearing — ClaimResult.item carries the DEAD run's identity while the stored row's owner_run_id becomes the resuming run (matches _plan_taken_over; verified in test_cas_fx.py); (2) pyarrow schema for ledger append must derive from the LIVE loaded table (field-id reassignment); (3) ledger.py has a private EMF _emit_metric print — your observability.py should become the shared EMF emitter and ledger.py a candidate first consumer (do not refactor ledger.py yourself if outside FILES; note it); (4) local_effects fixture in tests/conftest.py: moto S3/DynamoDB/EventBridge + SqlCatalog + sftp_store + clock_box + deterministic delivery-id counter. Read ingestion/.claude/agent-memory/senior-de/ for full notes.
verified+closed by coordinator. Notable deviations accepted: run_id threading into execute/record_nondelivery (fencing correctness — dead-run id would wedge resumed claims); registry_cache as explicit dict param (test isolation); no double content-hash computation; 3-part fixture per 15.2 over 12.4's generic wording. All journaled for critique gate.

title: [M2] Ledger + CAS factories, bootstrap, build_effects, and the local_effects fixture
description:
Complete the effect side and the local acceptance stack. `effects/ledger.py` make_ledger_fx (§7.7, D-7): injectable catalog via LedgerConfig (catalog_kind glue|sql; SqlCatalog with SQLite + local FS warehouse for tests); append builds a pyarrow table from DeliveryRecord rows and commits; on CommitFailedException retry with fresh table load up to 5 attempts, jittered backoff 0.5–8 s, LedgerCommitRetries metric per retry, then TransientError; scan_feed with row_filter on feed_id (+ received_at >= since) returning RAW rows always — folding is the caller's job. `effects/cas.py` make_cas_fx (§8.4 semantics normative): claim = PutItem full item with attribute_not_exists(pk) → WON; else consistent GetItem → LOST_COMPLETED / LOST_IN_PROGRESS (claimed within 1200 s) / stale → conditional UpdateItem takeover (owner_run_id = observed AND status = in_progress) → TAKEN_OVER, condition-failed → LOST_IN_PROGRESS; complete fenced on owner_run_id; sweep_stale (Scan with filter — table is tiny); marker_exists; mark (conditional put, True iff first writer, ttl_days=35). Item attributes exactly per §8.4 including objects_inventory JSON of StagedObjects and the trigger payload. `bootstrap/create_ledger.py` (§6.2, §9.4): idempotent create_table_if_not_exists with the full column list, partition spec identity(feed_id) + day(received_at), and Athena vacuum table properties set explicitly (vacuum_max_snapshot_age_seconds=2592000, vacuum_min_snapshots_to_keep=5 — Athena ignores history.expire.* and its 5 d default would silently shrink the audit window). `effects/build.py` build_effects(RuntimeConfig) → Effects — the ONLY production assembly point. `tests/conftest.py` per §12.5: the central `local_effects → Effects` fixture — same record shape production uses — from moto clients, a SqlCatalog ledger bootstrap-created via create_ledger.py (thereby testing the bootstrap), an in-memory sftp dict behind sftp_fx_for, a controllable now(), and a seeded deterministic new_delivery_id sequence. No mocking framework anywhere. Integration tests: full CAS state machine including fencing (a taken-over zombie cannot complete), takeover race condition-failure path, marker semantics; ledger append/scan round-trip, commit-retry path (inject a conflicting concurrent commit), bootstrap idempotence (run twice, no error, schema stable).

FILES (ownership): ingestion/ingestion/effects/ledger.py, ingestion/ingestion/effects/cas.py, ingestion/ingestion/effects/build.py, ingestion/ingestion/bootstrap/create_ledger.py, ingestion/tests/conftest.py, ingestion/tests/integration/test_ledger_fx.py, ingestion/tests/integration/test_cas_fx.py, ingestion/tests/integration/test_bootstrap.py
acceptance_criteria: `make test-integration` green (the M2 milestone gate): CAS WON/LOST_COMPLETED/LOST_IN_PROGRESS/TAKEN_OVER + fencing, ledger append/scan/retry, bootstrap idempotence; `make lint` green.

title: [M1] Folds, candidate selection, and the pure registration planners
description:
Implement the ledger read-model and all decision logic as pure functions. `core/folds.py` (§7.4 normative): latest_dispositions (group by delivery_id, max (recorded_at, disposition-rank); tie rank unreadable > superseded > duplicate > incomplete > registered), registered_deliveries, feed_watermark, acquired_final (every object INCLUDING role=manifest, for latest disposition in {registered, duplicate, superseded} — superseded stays acquired), observed_defective (single-object trailer/timer deliveries only; manifest-mode deliberately excluded — they are re-examined manifest-first each run). `core/windows.py` (§7.4): RemoteFile; select_candidates (fnmatch pattern → drop (name,bytes) ∈ acquired ∪ defective unless force → timer quiet-window filter → sort (mtime, name) ascending; force=True bypasses only step 2, D-16); select_manifests (non-final manifests re-examined every run by design). `core/decisions.py` (§8.3 normative, §8, §9.4): define RegistrationRequest here (§8.1 — its CompletenessResult field is why it lives here, not model.py), CopySpec, RegistrationPlan; plan_registration building plans per the claim.kind table — WON (registered row + superseded accretion row when a registered prior with same delivery_key and different content_hash exists in the fold of prior rows; copies from StagedObjects with src_key set; event; complete_claim), LOST_COMPLETED and LOST_IN_PROGRESS (one duplicate row each — both sides of every race are remembered, no event/copies), TAKEN_OVER (plan rebuilt entirely from claim.item — the dead run's delivery_id/received_at/inventory — byte-identical to what the dead run would have executed; supersession detection runs here too); every row obeys the §6.2 population table exactly. plan_nondelivery with the append-on-change rule (§8: latest row for this delivery_key has same disposition AND same observed (name,bytes) inventory → rows=(); never copies/event/claim). plan_reconciliation (§9.4 step 3: delivery_keys with >1 live registered → superseded accretion rows for all but newest received_at; idempotent). Do NOT attempt to fix the concurrent-correction race in the planner (§8.3: both racers may compute supersedes=None; reconciliation repairs it — a delivery_key lock was explicitly rejected). Unit tests: fold idempotence property latest_dispositions(rows+rows)==latest_dispositions(rows) (§12.3), rank tiebreak, acquired/defective set semantics, selection with force and quiet window, one plan test per claim.kind, append-on-change suppression, TAKEN_OVER identity adoption. Parallel with m1-core-verifiers — do not touch hashing/minting/completeness/expectations files.

FILES (ownership): ingestion/ingestion/core/folds.py, ingestion/ingestion/core/windows.py, ingestion/ingestion/core/decisions.py, ingestion/tests/unit/test_folds.py, ingestion/tests/unit/test_windows.py, ingestion/tests/unit/test_decisions.py
acceptance_criteria: `make test-unit` green including the fold-idempotence hypothesis property and one plan-content test per claim.kind (WON/LOST_COMPLETED/LOST_IN_PROGRESS/TAKEN_OVER); `make lint` green.

description:
Implement the effect-side interface and the non-ledger factories. `effects/records.py` (§7.7 verbatim — the dataclass definitions there are normative): ObjectSummary, StoreFx, LedgerFx, CasFx, SftpFx, Effects; also define TransientError here (the only exception type in the codebase, §7.3 — raised by effect functions only). NOTE, do not act on it: the M5 absence sweep will need an async Lambda-invoke capability §7.7 omits; it will be added additively by m5-absence — do NOT add it now. `ingestion/config.py` (§7.2): frozen RuntimeConfig + from_env reading CONVEYER_<UPPER_SNAKE> vars, failing loudly on absence. `effects/s3.py` make_store_fx: list_prefix; stream_sha256 (streaming, never spools to disk); get_bytes with max-bytes cap returning Defect when exceeded (manifest read, 1 MiB cap at call sites); get_tail via ranged GET; copy_verbatim server-side (multipart copy above 5 GiB); stream_upload (chunks in → multipart upload, sha256 accumulated en route → (hex, bytes); MUST abort the multipart upload on iterator failure — state lives inside one function activation, §7.7). `effects/events.py` make_event_fx: PutEvents to the bus, Source 'conveyer.ingestion', DetailType per model (§6.4); failure → TransientError. `effects/secrets.py` make_secret_fn: GetSecretValue → SftpSecret parse (§6.7). `effects/sftp.py` make_sftp_fx: paramiko closures — listdir returning RemoteFile values, read_chunks 1 MiB iterator; host_key_fingerprint verification when present, WARNING log on first-connection trust when null (§6.7); 30 s connect / 60 s read timeouts; failures → TransientError. Integration tests (factory level, §12.1) under moto for store/events/secrets: streaming hash correctness, multipart abort on failing iterator, get_bytes cap → Defect, tail read, event put. Real paramiko is not exercisable under moto — document that exclusion inline per §12.5 (the sftp path is covered by the in-memory record in golden tests). title: [M1] Core verifiers: hashing, minting, completeness functions, expectations + property tests
description:
Implement four pure core modules against the M0 model types. `core/hashing.py` (§6.5 normative algorithm): canonical_content_hash over (name, sha256_hex) pairs — sha256sum-style two-space lines, bytewise sort, sha256 of the joined utf-8 bytes, 'sha256:' prefix; manifest always excluded by the caller. `core/minting.py` (§6.6): the fixed CONVEYER_INGESTION_NS constant with the LLD-mandated comment that changing it re-mints every batch identity; mint_batch_id via uuid5 (linter-allowed). `core/completeness.py` — ADD the functions to the value-types file M0 created (§7.3 signatures normative): parse_manifest (bytes → ManifestV1 | Defect; this is the single linter-allowlisted try, catching ValidationError/UnicodeError only — see m0-purity-linter); evaluate_manifest (incomplete: declared file absent or byte-size mismatch; defective: feed_id mismatch, duplicate names in manifest, sha256 mismatch where observed sha256 is not None; asserted_record_count = sum only if ALL files declare one, else None); evaluate_trailer (decode last-4096-bytes tail utf-8 errors='replace'; final non-empty line must fullmatch spec.pattern; absent/malformed → incomplete 'trailer missing or malformed'; count_group present but non-integer → defective); quiet_window_satisfied. `core/expectations.py` (§7.5, D-11): expectation_dates, expected_by (zoneinfo wall-time localization — never fixed offsets; fold=0 defaults accepted), overdue_dates (lookback 3, qualification = registered received_at within the expected date's feed-tz day). Unit suite per §12.3: hypothesis property tests — canonical_content_hash invariance under object permutation + sensitivity to any name/hash change; mint_batch_id determinism; DST calendar pinned for America/New_York spring and fall transition dates; plus example-based tests for every completeness verdict branch. Everything pure: no I/O, no raise (except the allowlisted try), 'now' always a parameter. Do NOT implement folds, windows, or planners (parallel bead) and do NOT touch model.py.

title: [M0] Purity + idiom linter with self-tests
description:
Implement `tools/purity_linter.py` per LLD §12.2 (rule lists are normative) enforcing the §7.0/D-17 idiom. Stdlib `ast` walk over `ingestion/**/*.py` and `sources/**/*.py`. Two rule groups. PURITY (applies to `ingestion/core/**` and `sources/**`; effects/entrypoints exempt): banned imports — module or any submodule, including `from os.path import join` and aliased forms — boto3, botocore, pyiceberg, paramiko, requests, urllib, http, socket, subprocess, os, sys, io, pathlib, sqlite3, random, tempfile, threading, multiprocessing, time; banned calls (attribute-resolved best-effort): open, eval, exec, __import__, datetime.now/utcnow/today, date.today, uuid.uuid1, uuid.uuid4 (uuid5 allowed — 'now' is always a parameter); ban `raise` and `try` statements. IDIOM (applies to ALL of ingestion/** and sources/**, no exemptions): `class` statements banned unless @dataclass(frozen=True)-decorated, pydantic BaseModel subclass, or enum.Enum subclass (pydantic validators allowed); banned imports anywhere: toolz, cytoolz, returns, pyrsistent, funcy, effect, unittest.mock. Output `file:line:rule`, nonzero exit on any violation. CRITICAL DESIGN POINT: include exactly one hardcoded allowlist entry permitting the `try` in `ingestion/core/completeness.py::parse_manifest` — §7.3 names it 'the ONE place a pydantic exception is caught-and-reified' while §12.2 bans try in core; the allowlist is the smallest resolution of that contradiction. Hardcode it with a comment citing both sections; do NOT build a config/pragma mechanism. STATE: OQ-1/2/5/6 all ruled (four Accepted ADRs, invariants M/N/L/PS). Remaining for 007.1 completion: OQ-7 (rebuild exclusion owner), F-1/F-5/F-7 drafting, F-3 state-table half, 004.1 ledger erratum.
OQ-7 decision analysis recorded as ADR (Proposed): design/adr-oq7-rebuild-exclusion.md — input to F-7. Proposes Option D: NO mutual exclusion — the swap commits conditionally on the state snapshot captured at fact-pin (I-19 before_id idiom), straddling MERGEs keep I-11's serializable conflict-retry path; both writers lose LOUDLY; quiesce demotes to 008 efficiency runbook backed by the marker-table in-flight probe (DC-1/AE-7 disposition). Four refinements folded: (1) quiesce probe blind window NAMED in runbook guidance — marker presence begins at commit, land→apply invisible, clean probe ≠ quiet (harmless per RB-3, but an unnamed caveat = runbook overclaim); (2) harness gains the specific tie-idempotency variant as case (c): B committed before pin, folded after swap → re-MERGE must no-op on ordering ties (D-2/D-4 tie discipline asserted, not inherited); (3) REGISTERED QUESTION to F-7 checklist: a successful swap is a state change no batch-completed announced — 006 D-3 perception-contract question (rebuild-complete event vs rebuild marker rows); (4) validation 1 is an ADOPTION GATE: F-7 may not lean on RB-1/RB-2 mechanical claims until the kernel probe passes on the pinned stack; swap-as-MERGE fallback re-prices RB-3's alarm threshold. - Code does: spine/spine/stages/fold.py:123-127 skips the MERGE entirely when the batch's facts for a type are empty (rows_merged_by_table[t]=0, no fold_snapshot_ids key) — a value-based skip, not a presence guard.
- Consequence: None — an empty-source MERGE would only add a physical no-op snapshot; the projection matches §8.2's absent-key rule.
- Auditor recommendation: Accept with a §8.2 annotation naming the empty-source short-circuit.

### U-7 (unruled deviation) — COORDINATOR RULING: ACCEPT AS BUILT — I-23 content-pinned channel honoured; annotate §6.5 step 6
- LLD cite: §6.5 step 6 / F-10: 'the deploy step that renders the S-15 grants also emits the table→class inventory'
- Doc says: One deploy step renders grants and the inventory from the same declaration source.
- Code does: spine/spine/bootstrap/create_record_tables.py:562-564 emits table-classes.json from the bootstrap script; S-15 grants live in Terraform (spine/terraform/modules/spine-pipeline/iam.tf); spine/README.md step 5c sequences the two.
- Consequence: Two deploy steps from one spec; a stale inventory makes bind refuse loudly (co-effect-class-not-in-inventory), never silently.
- Auditor recommendation: Accept with an annotation (the I-23 content-pinned channel is honoured); optionally add a Terraform-side consistency check later.

### U-4 (unruled deviation) — COORDINATOR RULING: ACCEPT AS INTERIM — annotate §12 ledger field reuse (feed_id carries the state table; batch_id rebuild-<12hex>)
- LLD cite: §9.2 'retries are attempt-truth… ride the run ledger (the rebuild stage-vocabulary accretion registered to 004.1)'; §12 'until it lands, the EMF metric is the retry record, named as the interim'; §12 RebuildSwapRetries 'dimensioned by pipeline and state table'
- Doc says: Interim = EMF only; ledger rows await 004.1's rebuild stage vocabulary; metric dimensioned by pipeline and state table.
- Code does: spine/spine/effects/rebuild.py:184-214 writes RunFact(stage='rebuild', batch_id='rebuild-<12hex>', feed_id=<state table>, attempt_id=str(n)) per attempt (an interim beyond the LLD's EMF-only interim, recorded in the module docstring); rebuild.py:286 emits the state table under the dimension NAME feed_id.
- Consequence: Ledger rows with a non-UUIDv5 batch_id and a table name in feed_id; dashboards grouping by feed_id see table names. Additive and value-free.
- Auditor recommendation: Accept as interim with the 004.1 vocabulary row owing the purpose-built shape, or emit the metric now with extra_dims={'state_table': …} and note the ledger field reuse in a §12 annotation.

### D006-2 (unruled deviation) — COORDINATOR RULING: ACCEPT AS BUILT — timestamp(…)/ifnull are the same node kinds as admitted members; annotate §6.1/§6.2 (additive)
- LLD cite: §6.1 [EM-1] (typed-literal Cast carve-out admits DATE '…'/TIMESTAMP '…' and, by structural identity, date('…')); §6.2 conditional row (coalesce, nvl, nullif)
- Doc says: The allowed set is exactly the enumerated members; date('…') is admitted only because it is the same node as DATE '…'.
- Code does: check_grammar.py:149-151 admits `to` in {DATE, TIMESTAMP, TIMESTAMPTZ}, so timestamp('…') and the TIMESTAMP '…' -> TIMESTAMPTZ normalization accept; ifnull(...) parses to Coalesce and accepts. Both are pinned as accepts in tests/unit/test_check_grammar.py:154-162,180.
- Consequence: Two authorable spellings beyond the documented surface; both value-determined and semantically identical to admitted forms; G-08 has no ifnull / timestamp('…') engine row.
- Auditor recommendation: Ratify by erratum annotation at §6.1/§6.2 (additive — same node kinds as admitted members, cannot be excluded without a spelling predicate that would contradict the date('…') argument) and add the two G-08 rows; or rule that spelling predicates are wanted and add them with G-07 reject rows.

Also: A006-9(b) duplicate-alias discharge by S1 (annotate C1) if the wave-2 bead did not emit the code; 006.1 §13.1 G-08 wording "45/45" wherever the doc quotes a count.

title: sec.deferred: L-1..L-8 low-severity security batch
description: Eight LOW findings from the security gate, batched. L-1 vestibule keys flattened to basenames — partner can upload incoming/a/x.csv and incoming/b/x.csv, dict-by-name keeps one (ambiguity/shadowing, not forgery — sha256 still binds content); fix: reject keys with more than one segment after incoming/. L-3 SFTP host-key TOFU never persists, so every connection is first-connection trust (spec-mandated by 6.7 null-fingerprint path); fix is a spec change: require host_key_fingerprint or write the observed one back after first success. L-4 no S3 server access logging / CloudTrail data events on landing — cross-account partner writes unauditable after the 14d vestibule expiry. L-5 per-feed drivers have no reserved_concurrent_executions, so retries+operator invokes can starve the capped registrar; fix: 1 per driver. L-6 no permission boundaries on any of the five role shapes. L-7 absence/detector.py logs whole ClaimItem reprs at WARNING (being fixed opportunistically in conveyer-4ot.37; verify and drop from this batch if done). L-8 committed carrier-x secret_ref placeholder points at account 000000000000 — fails closed but the feed is non-functional until the runbook updates it and CI does not catch the mismatch; fix: have make registry cross-check the account id. Log-injection surface was audited CLEAN (all partner values formatted with %r).
